title: Finite signed elimination family and its necessary inequalities
statement:
Let $V$ be a $\mathbf Q$-vector space [def-weil-field], let $I$ be a finite set, let $f_i:V\to\mathbf Q$ be $\mathbf Q$-linear forms for $i\in I$, and let $v\in V$. Put $a_i=f_i(v)$ and $I_0=\{i\in I:a_i=0\}$, $I_+=\{i\in I:a_i>0\}$, $I_-=\{i\in I:a_i<0\}$. Define the family
$$\mathcal F=(f_h)_{h\in I_0}\sqcup(f_i)_{i\in I_+}\sqcup(a_i f_j-a_j f_i)_{(i,j)\in I_+\times I_-}.$$
Then $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of $\mathbf Q$-linear forms. For every $x\in V$ and $t\in\mathbf Q$, if $t\ge0$ and $f_i(x)-ta_i\ge0$ for all $i\in I$, then $g(x)\ge0$ for every member $g$ of $\mathcal F$. Empty index sets, repeated forms and zero forms are allowed.

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old proof steps 3--4 (explicit finite family and forward inclusion). Expose VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, supplies toric context only, not this assertion.

proof.text: The three sign classes $I_0,I_+,I_-$ are subsets of the finite set $I$, hence finite. The family is indexed by the disjoint union $J=I_0\sqcup I_+\sqcup(I_+\times I_-)$. Enumerating the two finite subsets and the finitely many pairs enumerates $J$, with $|J|=|I_0|+|I_+|+|I_+||I_-|$. Thus $\mathcal F$ is a finite indexed family; no distinctness of its values is asserted.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the forward elimination assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old steps 3--4. ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: The first two blocks consist of the given linear forms. For $(i,j)\in I_+\times I_-$ define $g_{ij}(z)=a_i f_j(z)-a_j f_i(z)$. For $y,z\in V$ and $q\in\mathbf Q$, linearity of $f_i,f_j$ and distributivity give $g_{ij}(y+z)=a_i(f_j(y)+f_j(z))-a_j(f_i(y)+f_i(z))=g_{ij}(y)+g_{ij}(z)$ and $g_{ij}(qz)=a_iq f_j(z)-a_jq f_i(z)=qg_{ij}(z)$. Hence each member is a rational linear form.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the forward elimination assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old steps 3--4. ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: Fix $x\in V$ and $t\ge0$ satisfying the residual inequalities. If $h\in I_0$, then $a_h=0$, so $f_h(x)=f_h(x)-ta_h\ge0$. If $i\in I_+$, then $a_i>0$, whence $ta_i\ge0$ and $f_i(x)=(f_i(x)-ta_i)+ta_i\ge0$. This verifies the first two blocks.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the forward elimination assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old steps 3--4. ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: If $(i,j)\in I_+\times I_-$, then $a_i>0$ and $-a_j>0$. Both residuals are nonnegative, so $a_i(f_j(x)-ta_j)+(-a_j)(f_i(x)-ta_i)\ge0$. Expanding and cancelling the terms $-ta_i a_j+ta_j a_i=0$ identifies this expression with $a_i f_j(x)-a_j f_i(x)=g_{ij}(x)$. This verifies the third block. Every index belongs to one of the three blocks, proving the required implication. Empty blocks impose no conditions, and the argument applies separately to every index even if its form repeats or is zero.
